# Cosimo by Medici & Company

> Grow your fund. Not your workload.

Cosimo is fund operations software from Medici & Company. It helps fund teams prepare draft investor reports, portfolio updates, and replies from the records they already keep. The website speaks to lean fund operations, finance, and investor-relations teams, with examples for real estate, venture capital, private equity, private credit, and hedge funds.

## How the proposed workflow fits a fund team

Start with the records behind one recurring task and an example of the output the team needs. Medici & Company configures and tests the workflow with the team, using its source records, reporting format, and review requirements. Drafts bring the figures and commentary together, with missing information and open questions marked for review. The fund team checks the work, resolves questions, approves the final version, and sends it through its usual process.

The website does not offer a universal integration list, fixed implementation time, quantified savings, security certification, or audit-readiness guarantee. Data handling, access, source systems, scope, and commercial terms need to be discussed for the fund's proposed setup.

## All-funds homepage

Path: /

The homepage introduces three recurring jobs: investor reporting, portfolio updates, and investor requests. An interactive example follows management accounts, company commentary, and a prior report format into a quarterly portfolio update.

The example uses Renaissance Capital, a fictional fund manager. Three companies report $27.0 million in quarterly revenue against a $27.5 million budget. One company's accounts show $6.0 million while its management update says $6.4 million. The draft uses the accounts provisionally and leaves the $400,000 difference visible for review. The example has inspectable source records and a three-page draft. It is authored demonstration content, not a live application run.

## Real estate

Path: /re/

The page focuses on quarterly LP reports, investor statements, capital call notices, and distribution notices. The reporting example uses property figures, manager updates, and investor capital records for fictional Renaissance Real Estate Fund I. Visitors can compare source records with the proposed draft and explore a six-page sample report.

The example preserves open property questions and shows a simplified capital-movement schedule. That schedule excludes income and valuation changes and is not a complete capital account statement. Investor notices use supplied, approved allocations; they do not execute payments.

## Venture capital

Path: /vc/

The page focuses on preparing portfolio and LP updates from founder submissions, company spreadsheets, and fund records. Its fictional Renaissance Venture Fund I example contains six companies, five current submissions, one stale submission, and a company with six months of runway at its reported burn rate. An unsigned financing discussion is not treated as cash received.

The six-page example includes portfolio metrics, cash and runway, founder commentary, capital movements, and open items. Company operating figures are not fund performance or valuation measures. The sample capital schedule is incomplete until the necessary approved allocations and adjustments are included.

## Private equity

Path: /pe/

The page focuses on bringing portfolio-company financials, management commentary, and fund records into reporting drafts. Its fictional Renaissance Buyout Fund I example compares company actuals with budgets and explains an EBITDA shortfall from supplied management notes. Unexplained variances and unapproved operating plans remain visible.

The six-page sample includes portfolio metrics, budget comparisons, company updates, capital movements, and review questions. The company totals are management-reported operating figures, not ownership-weighted fund results. The sample does not implement an ILPA reporting template or constitute a complete quarterly financial reporting package.

## Private credit

Path: /credit/

The page focuses on private credit and direct lending: borrower review packs, covenant worksheets, reporting follow-ups, and LP updates. Its fictional Renaissance Direct Lending Fund I example follows six loans through servicing data, supplied covenant calculations, and a reporting tracker.

One worksheet shows leverage of 4.80 times using submitted EBITDA and 5.33 times if an unresolved add-back is excluded, compared with a supplied maximum of 5.00 times. This is a review question, not a determination of compliance or default. Another item identifies a missing borrower certificate. Cash interest received and PIK accrued are shown separately; neither is presented as the fund's net return.

The six-page credit pack is an authored example. Agreement definitions, adjustments, testing dates, and exceptions require the credit team's review. Lending decisions remain with the team.

## Hedge funds

Path: /hedge/

The page focuses on investor letters, close-file exceptions, subscription/redemption activity, and allocator response drafts. Its fictional Bellosguardo Equity Fund example uses administrator-approved figures and supplied policy records for a long/short equity fund.

The six-page monthly pack separates investor-facing drafts from internal working papers. It includes class returns, an exposure snapshot, investor activity, a cash discrepancy, and a questionnaire response that needs current supporting evidence. The administrator retains responsibility for the official NAV; the fund team resolves exceptions and approves investor communications. The page does not claim to perform trading, investment decisions, complete risk management, or independent assurance.

## What the examples prove—and what they do not

All website records, commentary, and outputs are fictional and prewritten. Interactions let visitors inspect the proposed document workflow, source records, figures, and review questions. They are not recordings of Cosimo generating these outputs, successful production proof runs, or customer results.

The examples explain the intended work. They do not substantiate a guaranteed processing time, hours saved, universal accuracy, autonomous delivery, audit readiness, or integration coverage. These workflows need configuration and testing with the fund team before making fund-specific capability commitments.

## How to start

Email info@medici.ai with a few sentences about the report or process your team prepares, where the information comes from, and which part takes the most time. Medici & Company will work through a first workflow to test with the team. Scope and commercial terms are agreed before starting. The website does not promise a free pilot, a fixed pilot duration, or a particular implementation schedule.
